summary:
Scott had just now let me know you’d okayed FLOW MY TEARS. I’m very 

glad. 

As to the changes. Re: paragraph two in your letter; I will reconstruct the items involved, naturally. Thanks; I’m sorry these got muddled. Re: paragraph three of your letter, the Ruth Rae section, which I regard as the mid-section of the novel. Here is my felling about that. I will cut this section. I will go over it entirely and tighten. This is one process I am good at, tighten­ ing, when it’s necessary; even when I don’t desire it I still can do it with skill (years ago I had to do a lot of that for Ace Books; I remember one time Don Wollheim told me he’d buy a novel of mine if it ran exactly 6,000 lines. No more, no less; exactly. I got it down to that and he bought it.) What I feel here is that whatever the purely discursive value the material in that section has, there are other considerations to be taken into account. You mention movement, the pace of the novel; that is one, and I would on my own add reader interest, which is of course allied to marketing aspects. 

So I yield on this, as to cutting the Ruth Rae section—and in a sense it’s not yielding at all because some of the best writing I’ve done has been in collabora­ tion with a good editor, although his or her name hasn’t appeared on the printed piece. (Maxwell Perkins was before my time, but I read his collected let­ ters in my early days and they made an impression on me that surfaces every now and then.) I wonder if you know this:...
